news.title: Horizon Gold marks 10 years on ASX with strong results
news.summary:
Horizon Gold managing director and CEO Scott Williamson talked with Proactive about the latest high-grade drilling results from the Gum Creek Gold Project, the company's 10-year anniversary on the ASX and its plans to transition towards gold production.

Williamson highlighted the latest reverse circulation (RC) drilling results at Kingfisher, including an intercept of 42 metres at approximately 2.8 grams per tonne gold and a further intercept of 10 metres at more than 10 grams per tonne gold.

The results demonstrate the potential for mineralisation to extend north towards the Swan-Swift area, while drilling at Psi has highlighted a potential underground mining opportunity near the historical Amigo underground mine.

Williamson also reflected on Horizon Gold's first decade as an ASX-listed company, highlighting the addition of more than one million ounces of gold over the past five years and the company's focus on open pit mining and simple metallurgy.

Gum Creek currently hosts a 2.3-million-ounce gold resource, with Williamson reporting discovery costs of approximately $20 per ounce.

“Our discovery cost is around $20 per ounce,” Williamson said, highlighting the company's exploration efficiency as it advances towards production.

Looking ahead, Williamson discussed the potential to increase annual gold production beyond the company's base case of approximately 100,000 ounces and extend the current 10-year mine life, outlining a possible scenario in which Gum Creek could operate for 20 years.

The interview explores Horizon Gold's resource growth strategy, historical mining advantages and long-term ambitions for the Gum Creek Gold Project.
